text: What does a bullet through the liver do to me?

args.label: Gunshot wound to the liver
args.source: Own estimate of moderate haemorrhage (ATLS class II-III shock: heart rate rises, blood pressure falls, breathing quickens); not published model numbers.

feelings.label: Pain
feelings.cause: Torn liver capsule and blood irritating the belly lining

feelings.label: Lightheaded
feelings.cause: Blood loss lowers pressure reaching the brain

stops.label: Wound
stops.say: The bullet tears liver tissue and its blood vessels; the liver bleeds freely because it holds so much blood.

stops.label: Heart races
stops.say: With less blood returning, the heart beats faster and vessels tighten to hold pressure up.

stops.label: Kidneys save
stops.say: Blood is diverted from kidneys and gut to protect the brain and heart; urine nearly stops.

steps.title: The bullet's path
steps.say: In this example a bullet enters from the front and tears through the liver. The liver is full of blood, so its torn vessels bleed freely into the belly.

composed.caption: Torn liver bleeding into the belly
composed.basis: Textbook trauma surgery: the liver receives about a quarter of cardiac output, so injuries bleed heavily

steps.title: The lung is hit too
steps.say: This path also crosses your lower right lung. Air and blood can leak around the lung, so it can't fully expand and breathing gets harder.

composed.caption: Air and blood leaking around lung
composed.basis: Textbook thoracoabdominal trauma: haemothorax and pneumothorax after diaphragm-crossing wounds

steps.title: The heart races
steps.say: Less blood returns to the heart, so it speeds up, from about 78 to around 118 beats a minute here, while blood pressure sags.

steps.title: Saving the brain first
steps.say: Stress hormones clamp vessels to the kidneys, gut and skin, keeping blood for brain and heart. Urine almost stops; you may feel cold, clammy, thirsty and lightheaded.

closeup.basis: Own understanding of shock physiology: sympathetic vasoconstriction diverts flow from kidneys

steps.title: What saves you
steps.say: Clots form at the tear, but a badly torn liver rarely stops alone. Firm pressure, fast transport, transfusion and surgery to pack the liver save the person.

composed.caption: Clot and surgical packing slow bleeding
composed.basis: Damage-control surgery principles: perihepatic packing and transfusion control liver haemorrhage

lines.text: The liver holds a lot of blood, so a bullet through it causes heavy internal bleeding.
In this estimate your pulse climbs to about 118 and pressure drops within half an hour.
This path also nicks your right lung. Surgery and transfusion are what stop the bleeding.
